title: Beachhead (four converging threads)
source: Blueprint worked example (Nolan-style interleaved timeline), Section 4, expanded to four threads

threads.label: Winters, a home-front radio operator, tracking the evacuation by wireless

events.time_expr: barely a minute into the dogfight
events.text: Farrow scans the horizon from the cockpit, fuel gauge dropping fast.
Tanner has been dug into the sand for six days, waiting for a ship that never comes.
Dawson pushes his fishing boat out from the coast at first light, three hours from the beach.
He banks hard as a plane goes down below him, the fight barely a minute old.
He watches the mole get bombed for the third time that week.
He pulls a shivering pilot from the water, radio crackling with news from the beach.
Gliding now with the engine cut, he sees hundreds of men lined up on the sand below.

events.time_expr: one week after reaching the beach
events.text: Tanner finally boards a ship, one week after he first reached the beach.
Dawson's boat reaches the mole just as Tanner's ship is pulling away.

events.time_expr: before dawn, the morning of the dogfight
events.text: Farrow climbs into the cockpit before dawn, briefed on the thousands massed along a beach across the water.

events.time_expr: over the channel, minutes before contact
events.text: He crosses the channel at altitude, smoke already rising from the coastline ahead.
Farrow lines up a burst on an enemy fighter, tracer fire stitching the sky as another plane spins away trailing smoke.
He watches the coastline rise fast, the crowded sand now filling the whole of his windscreen.
The pilot braces in the cockpit as the sea rushes up grey and flat beneath him.
Farrow ditches just short of the sand, scrambling clear of the cockpit as the plane noses under.
He is hauled, dripping, over the gunwale of a small fishing boat, the whole ordeal over almost as soon as it began.
He queues at the water's edge for hours, watching ship after ship turn back under strafing fire.
He shares a tin of rations with a stranger, both of them trading rumors of a mole further down the beach.
Tanner helps drive stranded trucks out into the shallows, building a makeshift jetty at low tide.
He watches a destroyer go down just offshore, the tide afterward pushing wreckage back onto the sand.
Tanner is herded into an orderly line along the mole for the first time all week.
He is given a place near the front of the queue as darkness falls.
Word passes down the line the instant dawn breaks: ships have been spotted approaching the mole.
He steers around a drifting lifeboat, empty and half-swamped in the swell.
He spots the wreckage of a downed fighter bobbing in the water ahead.
Dawson changes course toward a lone figure waving from the waves.
The rescued pilot, wrapped in a blanket, points Dawson toward the mole where the crowds are thickest.
His boat joins a line of small craft ferrying men out to the larger ships, the work stretching on into the early afternoon.
He takes on a dozen soldiers, the little boat riding low and the fuel gauge sinking toward empty.
Dawson turns back toward the mole for one more run before the fuel runs out.
Winters logs the first garbled signal at the listening post: large numbers stranded, awaiting evacuation.
A bulletin crackles through describing repeated bombing runs on a mole somewhere near the beach.
Winters relays an urgent request for every available small craft to the Admiralty.
He hears of a destroyer lost just offshore and holds off telling the families waiting outside.

events.time_expr: day 7, the instant the dogfight opens
events.text: A burst of Morse reports fighters clashing in the skies above the beach, the signal almost drowned out by static.

events.time_expr: day 7, late morning into early afternoon
events.text: Word comes over the wireless that civilian boats are ferrying soldiers from the beach in growing numbers.
Winters hears, secondhand, that a downed pilot was fished alive out of the Channel.
A report notes that the queues on the mole are finally moving quickly.
Word arrives that the last ships have pulled away from the mole.
Winters logs the final tally of the day and switches off the set, the beach reportedly emptying at last.
